headline: Nvidia revenue hits $96.2B, memory commitments $160B as AI demand surges.
summary: Nvidia posted record $96.2 billion revenue, up 106% YoY, fueled by AI hardware demand. The company committed $160 billion for memory procurement, part of $279 billion in long-term supply pacts, to secure future AI growth.
details: Nvidia reported record revenue of $96.2 billion for Q2 FY2027, a 106% increase year-over-year. This surge was primarily driven by the escalating demand for its AI hardware across various sectors.
The company's net income reached $59.688 billion, marking a 126% YoY increase, with a robust gross margin of 75.0%. Sales from Compute & Networking hardware alone accounted for $88.299 billion.

CEO Jensen Huang stated that 'AI has reached its inflection point,' emphasizing that AI is now performing 'useful work' and that 'compute is revenue.' He noted accelerating demand and a 'golden age' for AI labs and startups.

Data center-grade AI hardware sales hit $89.023 billion, up 117% YoY. Hyperscalers contributed $48.710 billion, while AI Clouds, Industrial, and Enterprise segments grew faster, reaching $40.313 billion.

To meet future demand, Nvidia dramatically increased its long-term purchase commitments from $119 billion to $279 billion in Q2 FY2027. The bulk of these commitments, specifically $160 billion, is primarily related to the procurement of memory.

These massive commitments signal Nvidia's projection of sustained high demand for its data center AI products. Customer forecasts suggest demand could double next year, though Nvidia's supply chain is expected to support about 70% growth.

Huang acknowledged that unconstrained demand would be 'a lot, a lot higher' than current supply capabilities. He confirmed that supply will remain a bottleneck at least through FY2028, despite securing significant resources.

For Q3 FY2027, Nvidia anticipates revenue of approximately $108 billion, with a GAAP gross margin of around 74%. The outlook excludes data center compute revenue from China due to ongoing uncertainties.

headline: Vercel CLI overhaul adds DNS, domains, and project management
summary: Vercel's CLI now supports DNS record management, domain renewals, and project member operations, enabling full infrastructure automation directly from the terminal.
details: Vercel has significantly expanded its CLI capabilities, now allowing developers to manage DNS records, renew domains, and handle project member operations directly from the command line. These new features include JSON output flags for easy scripting.

This update addresses a crucial gap in infrastructure automation, enabling seamless integration into agent-driven deployment pipelines and CI steps. Developers no longer need to switch to the dashboard or create custom API wrappers for these tasks.

Separately, MiniMax M3 and M2.7 models are available for free via Vercel AI Gateway until September 6. Users are advised to configure fallback providers to avoid production incidents after the free period ends.

Vercel also introduced a new tracing feature that continuously samples live production traffic. It offers automatic instrumentation for infrastructure and fetch spans, with custom spans via @vercel/otel, priced at $0.50 per million span units.

The Vercel Sandbox now supports multiple regions (iad1, sfo1, cle1, cdg1), allowing developers to select regions via CLI or SDK. This improves latency for workloads sensitive to database or object store proximity.
Furthermore, Vercel Speed Insights now provides 10,000 Real User Monitoring (RUM) events per month for free across unlimited projects, a significant upgrade from its previous free tier model.
